data.name: Arindam
data.gender_notes: Arindam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arindam is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'arindamana', which means 'possessed by the gods'. In Hindu mythology, the name is given to a child believed to be chosen by the gods, often with special blessings and protection. The name Arindam carries the meaning “Possession of the gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arindam usually hope their child will grow to embody possession of the gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Arindam belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Possession of the gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arindam total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Arindam Chattopadhyaya was a renowned Indian philosopher and social scientist who was born on 8 May 1947 in Kolkata, India. He was a leading figure in the Indian Marxist-Leninist movement and is best known for his works on political theory and contemporary Indian society.

historical_references.reference: Arindam Agrahari was a famous Hindu scholar and philosopher who lived during the Gupta Empire period (circa 4th to 6th century AD). He is known for his contributions to the development of the Nyaya school of Indian philosophy, which focused on logic, epistemology, and metaphysics.
